sections.title: Get the band right: 920-926 MHz under the ACMA LIPD class licence
sections.intro: The single most expensive mistake in cross-border RFID sourcing is band mismatch. Australia's UHF RAIN band is 920-926 MHz, authorised under the ACMA Low Interference Potential Devices (LIPD) class licence at up to 4 W EIRP — it overlaps the top of the US 902-928 MHz band but sits nowhere near the EU 865-868 MHz band. Order 920-926 MHz tuning on the PO. (Access cards at 13.56 MHz are global and unaffected.)

sections.title: Landed cost: HS 8523.52, ChAFTA 0% duty and 10% GST
sections.intro: The unit price is the headline; the landed cost is the story. For Australia there are three characters — the HS line, the ChAFTA tariff preference, and the 10% GST.

dataHighlight.heading: RFID smart cards enter Australia duty-free under ChAFTA
dataHighlight.text: RFID cards and inlays classify under HS 8523.52 ("smart cards"). Under the China-Australia Free Trade Agreement (ChAFTA, in force since 2015) qualifying Chinese-origin goods enter at a 0% tariff, so the duty line is nil with a valid certificate of origin. What remains is the 10% Goods and Services Tax, charged on the landed value (goods + freight + insurance) at import and generally creditable for GST-registered businesses. On a DDP quote, freight, GST and clearance are all included in the price you see — no border surprises. Confirm the exact classification and any preference paperwork with your customs broker.

faq.question: Which UHF band do your tags use for Australia?
faq.answer: Australia's UHF RAIN band is 920-926 MHz under the ACMA LIPD class licence (up to 4 W EIRP), so we tune passive inlays for 920-926 MHz. EU 865-868 MHz inlays read short on an Australian portal and are not a drop-in. HF access-control cards at 13.56 MHz are globally harmonised and are unaffected by the UHF band — specify 920-926 MHz only for UHF inlay and label orders.

faq.question: Are your RFID cards compatible with Gallagher and Inner Range access control systems?
faq.answer: Yes. MIFARE Classic 1K cards work with the majority of existing Gallagher, Inner Range and legacy 13.56 MHz readers deployed across Australia, and DESFire EV3 (AES-128) is available for high-security sites. Because reader configurations vary, we ship free sample cards to your Australian address so you can confirm compatibility on your live readers before any bulk order.

faq.question: How do Australian GST and import duties work on an order?
faq.answer: RFID smart cards classify under HS 8523.52 and qualify for a 0% tariff under the China-Australia Free Trade Agreement (ChAFTA) with a valid certificate of origin. The 10% GST applies on the landed value at import and is generally creditable for a GST-registered business. On a DDP quote, freight, GST and clearance are included in the price up front — confirm the classification and preference paperwork with your customs broker.

faq.question: What is the total delivery time to Australia including production?
faq.answer: A typical first order runs about 10-17 days end to end: samples in the first few days, 3-10 days production and read-testing, then 5-7 business days express air to Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth or Adelaide. Bulk programmes on sea freight take longer and are planned against a blanket agreement.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity for Australian buyers?
faq.answer: MOQ depends on the product and personalisation and is quoted per order with your target card or inlay, artwork and annual volume. Samples for compatibility testing are available before any commitment — request them with your reader model and use-case.

faq.question: Can I get samples before placing a large order?
faq.answer: Yes. Free sample kits ship to Australian addresses so you can test read performance and reader compatibility on your own hardware first. For UHF orders the samples are 920-926 MHz-tuned so the test reflects Australian field conditions.

brief.label: Australian band and radio rules
brief.text: UHF RFID in Australia operates at 920-926 MHz under the ACMA Low Interference Potential Devices (LIPD) class licence, at up to 4 W EIRP with frequency hopping. Passive inlays must be antenna-tuned for 920-926 MHz; EU 865-868 MHz inlays underperform. Radio devices carry RCM (Regulatory Compliance Mark) compliance to AS/NZS 4268. HF access cards at 13.56 MHz are globally harmonised and unaffected.

brief.label: Compliance and data
brief.text: The RCM covers electrical and radio compliance for equipment supplied into Australia; readers carry it, passive tags are field devices. Credential and cardholder data falls under the Privacy Act 1988 (Australian Privacy Principles).

brief.label: Landed cost
brief.text: RFID smart cards classify under HS 8523.52 and enter Australia at 0% tariff under the China-Australia Free Trade Agreement (ChAFTA); 10% GST applies on the landed value at import. Incoterms EXW or DDP; DDP includes freight, GST and clearance.

brief.label: Logistics
brief.text: Express air via DHL/FedEx from Shenzhen to Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth and Adelaide in 5-7 business days; sea freight for bulk. Free sample kits ship to Australian addresses for reader-compatibility testing before a bulk order.
